classified_spans.text:
Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the codebase. Here is my thorough report. --- ## Thorough Exploration Report: Learner Progress Tracking in the Tutors Platform ### 1. CourseVisit and localStorage Profile **File:** `src/lib/services/connect/services/localStorageProfile.ts` The `CourseVisit` type is defined at `src/lib/services/connect/types.ts` (lines 9-19): ```typescript export type CourseVisit = { id: string; title: string; img?: string; icon?: IconType; lastVisit: string; credits: string; visits?: number; private: boolean; favourite: boolean; }; ``` **What is stored per course:** Only metadata -- the course ID, title, image/icon, last visit timestamp, credits string, total visit count, private flag, and favourite flag. There is NO per-LO progress or completion tracking in `CourseVisit`. **How visits are loaded/saved:** - Stored under `localStorage.courseVisits` as a JSON-serialized array of `CourseVisit` objects. - `reload()` reads from `localStorage.courseVisits` and parses JSON. - `save()` writes the in-memory `courseVisits` array back via `JSON.stringify`. - `logCourseVisit(course)` increments `visits` and updates `lastVisit` if the course already exists; otherwise prepends a new record. - `deleteCourseVisit`, `favouriteCourse`, `unfavouriteCourse` all follow the same reload-then-save pattern. **ProfileStore interface** (`types.ts` lines 24-35) is the abstraction both storage backends implement: ```typescript export interface ProfileStore { courseVisits: CourseVisit[]; reload(): void; save(): void; logCourseVisit(course: Course): void; favouriteCourse(courseId: string): void; unfavouriteCourse(courseId: string): void; deleteCourseVisit(courseId: string): void; getCourseVisits(): Promise; } ``` ### 2. Supabase Profile **File:** `src/lib/services/connect/services/supabaseProfile.svelte.ts` The Supabase profile implements the same `ProfileStore` interface but stores data in the `tutors-connect-profiles` Supabase table. It uses the `tutorsId.value?.login` (GitHub login) as the key: - **Table:** `tutors-connect-profiles`, columns: `tutorId` (text PK), `profile` (jsonb -- serialized `CourseVisit[]`). - `reload()`: `supabase.from("tutors-connect-profiles").select("profile").eq("tutorId", login)` -- reads the full profile JSON blob. - `save()`: `supabase.from("tutors-connect-profiles").upsert({ tutorId: login, profile: this.courseVisits })` -- writes the entire array as a single jsonb column. **Profile sync between localStorage and Supabase:** The sync is implemented in `src/lib/services/connect/services/connect.svelte.ts`. The `tutorsConnectService` object starts with `profile: localStorageProfile` (line 42). When a user authenticates via `reconnect(user)`, it switches to `this.profile = supabaseProfile` (line 68). There is no explicit merge/sync -- when unauthenticated, localStorage is the storage backend; when authenticated, Supabase is. They both store the same `CourseVisit[]` structure. localStorage data is NOT migrated to Supabase on sign-in. **Other Supabase tables used for course tracking** (from `allCourseAccess.ts`): - `tutors-connect-courses`: global course visit statistics (course_id, visited_at, visit_count, course_record). Updated on every course visit via `updateCourseList(course)`. - `tutors-connect-users`: student profile data (github_id, avatar_url, full_name, email, date_last_accessed, sentiment, online_status). ### 3. Learning Records / Analytics / Time Tracking **Key files:** - `src/lib/services/community/services/analytics.svelte.ts` - `src/lib/services/community/utils/supabase-client.ts` - `node_modules/@tutors/tutors-time-lib/src/` (the external time analysis library) **How events are recorded when a learner visits an LO:** The flow begins in `connect.svelte.ts` at the `learningEvent(params)` method (line 183): 1. Called with params (may contain `loid`). 2. Calls `analyticsService.learningEvent(currentCourse, params, currentLo, tutorsId)`. 3. In `analytics.svelte.ts`, this determines the `loRoute` (line 27-33) and calls `reportPageLoad`. 4. `reportPageLoad` calls `storeStudentCourseLearningObjectInSupabase(course, loRoute, lo, student)`. 5. In `supabase-client.ts`, this calls `handleInteractionData` then `insertOrUpdateCalendar`. **The `learning_records` Supabase table** (composite key: `student_id, course_id, lo_id`): ``` course_id: string student_id: string (GitHub login) lo_id: string (the LO route) duration: number (in 30-second increments, converted to minutes on read) count: number (page load count) date_last_accessed: timestamptz type: string (LO type: "lab", "talk", etc.) ``` **Duration tracking:** The `startTimer()` method in `connect.svelte.ts` (line 198) sets up a `setInterval` every 30 seconds that calls `analyticsService.updatePageCount`. This calls `updateLearningRecordsDuration` which uses a Supabase RPC `increment_calendar` / `get_count_learning_records` to increment the duration counter. Each tick = +1 (representing 30 seconds). **The `calendar` Supabase table** (composite key: `id, studentid, courseid`): ``` id: string (date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD) studentid: string courseid: string timeactive: number (in 30-second blocks, converted to minutes on read) pageloads: number ``` **The `tutors-time-lib`** provides read-only analysis: - `CourseTime.getAllLearningRecordsForCourse(courseId)` fetches all `learning_records` for a course. - `CourseTime.getCalendarData(courseId)` fetches all `calendar` rows for a course. - `BaseLabModel` pivots learning records into per-student lab rows. - `BaseCalendarModel` pivots calendar entries into day/week views. - The `LearningRecord` type from the time lib (`node_modules/@tutors/tutors-time-lib/src/types/lab-types.ts`) mirrors the DB schema. **Important:** The `Lo` type has a `learningRecords?: Map` field (line 39 of `learning-objects.ts`), but a grep shows this field is never populated anywhere in the current codebase. It is a vestigial/placeholder field. ### 4. Course Tree and LO Traversal **Key files:** - `src/lib/services/course/services/lo-tree.ts` (app-level tree decoration) - `node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/utils/lo-utils.ts` (core tree utilities) - `node_modules/@tutors/tutors-model-lib/src/services/lo-tree.ts` (model lib tree decoration) **How the course tree is built:** 1. A course is loaded as JSON from `{courseUrl}/tutors.json` (in `course.svelte.ts` line 42). 2. `decorateCourseTree(course, courseId, courseUrl)` is called (from `lo-tree.ts` line 28). 3. `flattenLos(course.los)` recursively collects all LOs into a flat array. The function (from `lo-utils.ts` line 22): ```typescript export function flattenLos(los: Lo[]): Lo[] { let result: Lo[] = []; los.forEach((lo) => { result.push(lo); if ("los" in lo) { result = result.concat(flattenLos(lo.los)); } }); return result; } ``` 4. Routes are injected, unknown LOs removed, then `decorateLoTree` recursively processes: - Sets `parentCourse`, loads icons, builds breadcrumbs. - For composite LOs (checked via `isCompositeLo` which tests `loCompositeTypes = ["unit", "side", "topic", "course"]`), it: - Builds `panels` (panelVideos, panelTalks, panelNotes, panelPodcasts). - Builds `units` (units, sides, standardLos). - Builds `toc` array (all child LOs flattened into a table-of-contents list). 5. Two indexes are built on the course object: - `course.loIndex: Map` -- maps route to Lo for ALL LOs. - `course.topicIndex: Map` -- maps route to Topic for topic LOs only. **Getting a flat list of all "leaf" LOs:** Yes, this can be done with existing utilities: ```typescript import { flattenLos, simpleTypes } from "@tutors/tutors-model-lib"; const allLos = flattenLos(course.los); const leafLos = allLos.filter(lo => simpleTypes.includes(lo.type)); ``` Where `simpleTypes` includes: `"note", "archive", "web", "github", "panelnote", "paneltalk", "panelvideo", "podcast", "talk", "book", "lab", "tutorial"`. Alternatively, use `filterByType(course.los, "lab")` to get just labs, etc. The `course.loIndex` map also provides direct route-to-Lo lookup for all LOs. ### 5. Course Card UI **Key files:** - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Card.svelte` -- the single card component - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Cards.svelte` -- renders a grid of Card components - `src/routes/(home)/CourseVisitCard.svelte` -- the dashboard course visit card - `src/routes/(home)/CourseList.svelte` -- the dashboard course list page **Card.svelte** accepts `cardDetails: CardDetails` and `cardLayout?: CardConfig` as props. The `CardDetails` interface (from `src/lib/services/themes/types.ts`): ```typescript export interface CardDetails { route: string; title?: string; type: string; summary?: string; summaryEx?: string; icon?: IconType; img?: string; student?: LoUser; video?: string; metric?: string; } ``` **Where a progress indicator would fit:** For the **dashboard/home view** (`CourseVisitCard.svelte`): This card already shows `courseVisit.visits` and `lastVisit`. A progress ring/bar could be added to the right section (lines 24-29) alongside the course icon/image, or in the footer area. The card is a simple `
` with a flex layout. For the **in-course Card.svelte**: The card has three layout modes: - **Portrait** (lines 112-122): header + figure + content. A progress ring could wrap the figure or sit in the header area. - **Landscape** (lines 138-147): left figure + right header/content. There is a `metric` field on `CardDetails` that renders at the bottom-right corner (line 146: `
{cardDetails.metric}
`). This `metric` slot is already an ideal place for a progress percentage or completion indicator. - **Circular** (lines 124-136): centered figure with title and icon. **Cards.svelte** maps `Lo` objects to `CardDetails` at line 57-64: ```typescript cardDetails={{ route: lo.route, title: lo.title, type: lo.type, summary: lo.summary, img: lo.img, icon: lo.icon, video: lo.video }} ``` Note that `metric` is not currently passed. Adding it here would populate the existing metric slot in landscape view. ### 6. Tree View / TOC Sidebar **Key files:** - `src/lib/ui/navigators/buttons/TocButton.svelte` -- button that opens the sidebar - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/structure/CourseContext.svelte` -- wrapper that passes `currentCourse` to the tree - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/structure/LoContextTree.svelte` -- the actual TreeView component - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/structure/LoContext.svelte` -- recursive list-based TOC (legacy) - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/structure/LoReference.svelte` -- renders a single item in the TOC **LoContextTree.svelte** uses `@skeletonlabs/skeleton-svelte`'s `TreeView` component. It builds nodes from the `lo.toc` array using `mapLoToNode`. Each tree item renders `LoReference` which shows an icon + title link. **Can visited/unvisited items be styled differently?** Yes, and here is how: The `LoReference.svelte` component (at `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/structure/LoReference.svelte`) is the leaf renderer. It currently renders a simple flex div with an icon and title. To style visited/unvisited items differently: 1. Pass a `visited` or `progress` status to `LoReference` (e.g., via the `Lo` object or a separate reactive store). 2. Conditionally apply CSS classes in `LoReference.svelte` (e.g., `opacity-50` for unvisited, a checkmark icon for visited). The `LoContextTree.svelte` could also be extended -- the `TreeView.BranchText` and `TreeView.Item` wrappers support custom classes. For example, a visited branch could get a green indicator dot or a struck-through title. The tree is already structured to know each `Lo` object per node (`node.lo`), so checking whether `lo.route` exists in a visited-LOs set would be straightforward. ### 7. Svelte 5 Runes and Reactivity Model **File:** `src/lib/runes.svelte.ts` The codebase uses Svelte 5 extensively. The core reactivity pattern is a custom `rune()` factory: ```typescript export const rune = (initialValue: T) => { let _rune = $state(initialValue); return { get value() { return _rune; }, set value(v: T) { _rune = v; } }; }; ``` This creates a reactive box with `.value` getter/setter. Used for global app state: - `currentCourse = rune(null)` - `currentLo = rune(null)` - `tutorsId = rune(null)` - `courseProtocol = rune("https://")` **Svelte 5 rune usage across the codebase** (30+ files confirmed using `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`): - `$props()` -- used in all components for prop declarations (e.g., `Card.svelte` line 11) - `$state()` -- used for reactive local state (e.g., `Cards.svelte` lines 19-21, `LoContextTree.svelte` line 40) - `$derived` / `$derived.by()` -- used for computed values (e.g., `Card.svelte` lines 18, 35-52) - `$effect()` -- used for side effects (e.g., `time/[courseid]/+page.svelte` line 19) - The `LoRecord` class in `src/lib/services/community/types.svelte.ts` uses `$state()` for class fields (lines 19-28), demonstrating reactive classes. **Services use the `rune()` pattern** rather than raw `$state`: - `themeService.layout = rune("expanded")` - `themeService.cardStyle = rune("portrait")` This approach allows services (plain `.ts` files, not `.svelte` files) to hold reactive state, provided the file has the `.svelte.ts` extension for Svelte 5 compilation. --- ### Summary of Key Architectural Observations for Progress Tracking 1. **No per-LO progress tracking exists currently.** `CourseVisit` only tracks course-level visit count. The `learning_records` table tracks time and visit counts per LO but only for authenticated users, and this data is NOT used to compute a progress/completion percentage anywhere. 2. **The data to compute progress already exists** in the `learning_records` Supabase table (keyed by `student_id, course_id, lo_id`). pairs.prompt_text:
I need to understand how to add learner progress tracking to the Tutors platform. Explore these areas very thoroughly:

1. **CourseVisit and localStorage profile**: Find `src/lib/services/connect/services/localStorageProfile.ts` and understand how course visits are tracked. What data is stored per course? What's the `CourseVisit` type? How are visits loaded/saved?

2. **Supabase profile**: Find `src/lib/services/connect/services/supabaseProfile.svelte.ts` or similar. How does the authenticated profile store data? What tables are used? How does the profile sync work between localStorage and Supabase?

3. **Learning records**: How does the time tracking / learning event system work? What data gets recorded when a learner visits an LO? Look at the analytics/events system.

4. **Course tree and LO traversal**: Look at `src/lib/services/course/services/lo-tree.ts` — how is the course tree built? How are all LOs in a course enumerated? Is there a way to get a flat list of all "leaf" LOs (labs, talks, notes, etc.) in a course?

5. **Course card UI**: Look at the course card components in `src/lib/ui/` — what card components exist, and where would a progress indicator (ring/bar) fit? Check both the catalogue/dashboard view and the in-course view.

6. **Tree view / TOC sidebar**: Look at how the table of contents / tree view sidebar renders. Could visited/unvisited items be styled differently?

7. **Existing Svelte 5 patterns**: Check if the codebase uses Svelte 5 runes ($state, $derived, $effect). What's the reactivity model?

Now let me look at the model library to find `flattenLos`, the Lo type definitions, and examine the CourseVisitCard and LoReference components, plus the dashboard/catalogue views. The model lib is an external JSR package. Let me search for it across node_modules and also look at the LLMs route that uses `flattenLos` and `filterByType` to understand how they work. The model library is an external JSR package. Let me check main repo or find the source. Now let me check the `CardDetails` type, the theme service (card styles), the `allCourseAccess` utility, and a few more remaining pieces. Now let me look at the `learningRecords` field on the Lo type, and also check the time-related components and the tutors-time-lib. Let me also look at the LearningRecord type from the time lib, and how the time route page fetches/displays data. Let me look at the Sidebar component and a few more Svelte 5 pattern examples to round out the analysis. Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the codebase. Here is my thorough report. --- ## Thorough Exploration Report: Learner Progress Tracking in the Tutors Platform ### 1. CourseVisit and localStorage Profile **File:** `src/lib/services/connect/services/localStorageProfile.ts` The `CourseVisit` type is defined at `src/lib/services/connect/types.ts` (lines 9-19): ```typescript export type CourseVisit = { id: string; title: string; img?: string; icon?: IconType; lastVisit: string; credits: string; visits?: number; private: boolean; favourite: boolean; }; ``` **What is stored per course:** Only metadata -- the course ID, title, image/icon, last visit timestamp, credits string, total visit count, private flag, and favourite flag. There is NO per-LO progress or completion tracking in `CourseVisit`. **How visits are loaded/saved:** - Stored under `localStorage.courseVisits` as a JSON-serialized array of `CourseVisit` objects. - `reload()` reads from `localStorage.courseVisits` and parses JSON. - `save()` writes the in-memory `courseVisits` array back via `JSON.stringify`. - `logCourseVisit(course)` increments `visits` and updates `lastVisit` if the course already exists; otherwise prepends a new record. - `deleteCourseVisit`, `favouriteCourse`, `unfavouriteCourse` all follow the same reload-then-save pattern. **ProfileStore interface** (`types.ts` lines 24-35) is the abstraction both storage backends implement: ```typescript export interface ProfileStore { courseVisits: CourseVisit[]; reload(): void; save(): void; logCourseVisit(course: Course): void; favouriteCourse(courseId: string): void; unfavouriteCourse(courseId: string): void; deleteCourseVisit(courseId: string): void; getCourseVisits(): Promise; } ``` ### 2. Supabase Profile **File:** `src/lib/services/connect/services/supabaseProfile.svelte.ts` The Supabase profile implements the same `ProfileStore` interface but stores data in the `tutors-connect-profiles` Supabase table. It uses the `tutorsId.value?.login` (GitHub login) as the key: - **Table:** `tutors-connect-profiles`, columns: `tutorId` (text PK), `profile` (jsonb -- serialized `CourseVisit[]`). - `reload()`: `supabase.from("tutors-connect-profiles").select("profile").eq("tutorId", login)` -- reads the full profile JSON blob. - `save()`: `supabase.from("tutors-connect-profiles").upsert({ tutorId: login, profile: this.courseVisits })` -- writes the entire array as a single jsonb column. **Profile sync between localStorage and Supabase:** The sync is implemented in `src/lib/services/connect/services/connect.svelte.ts`. The `tutorsConnectService` object starts with `profile: localStorageProfile` (line 42). When a user authenticates via `reconnect(user)`, it switches to `this.profile = supabaseProfile` (line 68). There is no explicit merge/sync -- when unauthenticated, localStorage is the storage backend; when authenticated, Supabase is. They both store the same `CourseVisit[]` structure. localStorage data is NOT migrated to Supabase on sign-in. **Other Supabase tables used for course tracking** (from `allCourseAccess.ts`): - `tutors-connect-courses`: global course visit statistics (course_id, visited_at, visit_count, course_record). Updated on every course visit via `updateCourseList(course)`. - `tutors-connect-users`: student profile data (github_id, avatar_url, full_name, email, date_last_accessed, sentiment, online_status). ### 3. Learning Records / Analytics / Time Tracking **Key files:** - `src/lib/services/community/services/analytics.svelte.ts` - `src/lib/services/community/utils/supabase-client.ts` - `node_modules/@tutors/tutors-time-lib/src/` (the external time analysis library) **How events are recorded when a learner visits an LO:** The flow begins in `connect.svelte.ts` at the `learningEvent(params)` method (line 183): 1. Called with params (may contain `loid`). 2. Calls `analyticsService.learningEvent(currentCourse, params, currentLo, tutorsId)`. 3. In `analytics.svelte.ts`, this determines the `loRoute` (line 27-33) and calls `reportPageLoad`. 4. `reportPageLoad` calls `storeStudentCourseLearningObjectInSupabase(course, loRoute, lo, student)`. 5. In `supabase-client.ts`, this calls `handleInteractionData` then `insertOrUpdateCalendar`. **The `learning_records` Supabase table** (composite key: `student_id, course_id, lo_id`): ``` course_id: string student_id: string (GitHub login) lo_id: string (the LO route) duration: number (in 30-second increments, converted to minutes on read) count: number (page load count) date_last_accessed: timestamptz type: string (LO type: "lab", "talk", etc.) ``` **Duration tracking:** The `startTimer()` method in `connect.svelte.ts` (line 198) sets up a `setInterval` every 30 seconds that calls `analyticsService.updatePageCount`. This calls `updateLearningRecordsDuration` which uses a Supabase RPC `increment_calendar` / `get_count_learning_records` to increment the duration counter. Each tick = +1 (representing 30 seconds). **The `calendar` Supabase table** (composite key: `id, studentid, courseid`): ``` id: string (date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD) studentid: string courseid: string timeactive: number (in 30-second blocks, converted to minutes on read) pageloads: number ``` **The `tutors-time-lib`** provides read-only analysis: - `CourseTime.getAllLearningRecordsForCourse(courseId)` fetches all `learning_records` for a course. - `CourseTime.getCalendarData(courseId)` fetches all `calendar` rows for a course. - `BaseLabModel` pivots learning records into per-student lab rows. - `BaseCalendarModel` pivots calendar entries into day/week views. - The `LearningRecord` type from the time lib (`node_modules/@tutors/tutors-time-lib/src/types/lab-types.ts`) mirrors the DB schema. **Important:** The `Lo` type has a `learningRecords?: Map` field (line 39 of `learning-objects.ts`), but a grep shows this field is never populated anywhere in the current codebase. Alternatively, use `filterByType(course.los, "lab")` to get just labs, etc. The `course.loIndex` map also provides direct route-to-Lo lookup for all LOs. ### 5. Course Card UI **Key files:** - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Card.svelte` -- the single card component - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Cards.svelte` -- renders a grid of Card components - `src/routes/(home)/CourseVisitCard.svelte` -- the dashboard course visit card - `src/routes/(home)/CourseList.svelte` -- the dashboard course list page **Card.svelte** accepts `cardDetails: CardDetails` and `cardLayout?: CardConfig` as props. The `CardDetails` interface (from `src/lib/services/themes/types.ts`): ```typescript export interface CardDetails { route: string; title?: string; type: string; summary?: string; summaryEx?: string; icon?: IconType; img?: string; student?: LoUser; video?: string; metric?: string; } ``` **Where a progress indicator would fit:** For the **dashboard/home view** (`CourseVisitCard.svelte`): This card already shows `courseVisit.visits` and `lastVisit`. A progress ring/bar could be added to the right section (lines 24-29) alongside the course icon/image, or in the footer area. The card is a simple `

A progress ring could wrap the figure or sit in the header area. - **Landscape** (lines 138-147): left figure + right header/content. {cardDetails.metric}
`). Pass a `visited` or `progress` status to `LoReference` (e.g., via the `Lo` object or a separate reactive store). 2. Conditionally apply CSS classes in `LoReference.svelte` (e.g., `opacity-50` for unvisited, a checkmark icon for visited). The tree is already structured to know each `Lo` object per node (`node.lo`), so checking whether `lo.route` exists in a visited-LOs set would be straightforward. ### 7.
